newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's TSUM shop sells most share issue.
newsitem.headline: Russia's TSUM shop sells most share issue.

text.p: Retailer OAO Torgovy Dom TSUM has placed most of its $11 million share issue aimed at funding its modernisation programme, lead manager OLMA said on Monday.
The company had received money for around 65 percent of the issue and had bids for more, project manager Svetlana Bik told Reuters.
"I am absolutely sure the issue will be fully sold in time," Bik said.
The 30 million shares, offered at 2,000 roubles each, will be on sale until December 31, 1996.
French bank Societe General is the agent for the issue.
OLMA said in a statement that households and several companies, including foreign ones, had become new TSUM shareholders.
The offer will help fund a $22 million reconstruction project with the rest of the money coming from bank loans and TSUM's cash flow.

The Moscow city government is TSUM's biggest shareholder with a 24.5 percent stake, Swiss private bank Pictet & Cie has 6.71 percent, OLMA has 5.03 percent, and AOOT Russ-Invest, a Russian investment fund, about 5.5 percent.
TSUM shares closed at $0.365 on Friday. The stock had not been traded on Monday at 1130 GMT.
